scope: All original evaluator payloads and required metadata-wrapped predictions; no scoring or semantic review.
limitations: No native video input: timestamped extracted frames are the actual perceptual input, unlike native-video API benchmarking.
No available audio perception/transcription tool; audio unassessed for all clips; spoken_dialogue is fail-open true.
Contact sheets use 640x360 maximum thumbnails, with original-resolution individual frames and original video available for denser inspection.
Frame labels use nominal ffmpeg fps filter output times; source-frame selection is quantized within a sampling interval.
Sparse visual sampling may miss events between sampled frames, especially the long clip at 1 fps; contact-sheet input is not equivalent to native-video perception.
Fresh delegated prompts restricted source access, but the shared filesystem was not sandboxed per task and tool-read access was not independently audited.
media_adaptations: Allowed frame fallback used: timestamped JPEG contact sheets via view_image rather than native-video input.
Thirteen short clips sampled at 4 fps; clip-01 sampled at 1 fps plus detected shot-boundary frames. These samples cannot guarantee coverage of every between-frame event.
All clips contain audio streams, but no honest audio-perception/transcription capability was available. Audio remained unassessed; spoken_dialogue=true triggered all 42 audio-role calls.

Shared contact sheets have at most 640x360 pixels per frame; native-resolution extracted JPEGs and the assigned MP4 were available for optional denser inspection. Individual tool reads were not independently audited.
Timestamp labels are nominal ffmpeg sampling times; exact source-frame selection is quantized.
